text:
incident-bot: ALERT: P2 - possible privacy exposure detected by task-runner. Auto-paging oncall. Incident ID: INC-2026-0427. Summary: elevated error rate + suspicious S3 acl change detected.

Arun: I’m oncall, acknowledging. Jumping in now.

Mike: grabbing logs and the short timeline. Seen a spike at ~14:02 UTC, request path /v1/embeddings, repeated 403->500 chain, then an S3 permission change triggered by automation.

Arun: okay first priorities: 1) isolate automated job that modified the bucket ACLs, 2) confirm any customer data in the affected bucket(s), 3) page sec and legal.

Jenna: I’m here (security). tagging @Legal-Bot for required disclosure guidance. What buckets?

Mike: bucket ids: redwood-embeds-prod-us-west-2-01 and redwood-temp-cache. Suspect the embed retryer job (embed-retryer-3) triggered a misconfigured role.

Arun: I’m detaching the role from the retryer now. Running:
```
aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name embed-retryer-3 --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AllowS3FullAccess
kubectl scale deployment embed-retryer-3 -n inference --replicas=0
```

Arun: done. Job scaled to 0. Network egress blocked to S3 for that pod.

Dave: support here. Do we have a list of customers who might be in those buckets? We might need immediate outreach.

Mike: running a prefix scan to map keys to customers. ETA ~8-10m. Using keys->customer mapping table.

Jenna: quick scope guidance: until we confirm, treat this as potential exposure. Prepare external wording that is explicit but conservative. We may need to disclose to affected customers and possibly regulators depending on PII.

Sara: I can start a staged customer notification draft. Will propose two versions: (1) short alert to potentially affected customers, (2) full incident notice once scope confirmed.

Arun: good. Also status page: small-status update now (investigating), followed by detailed update in 60m or after scope. Someone take it?

Mike: I’ll post the status page update. Proposed text (short):
"Status: We are investigating an incident affecting some embedding requests and a related storage ACL change. We have isolated the automation and are assessing the scope. No confirmed customer impact at this time."

Jenna: approved for interim. Add ETA for next update: 60 minutes.

incident-bot: NOTE: handoff scheduled in 30m at 1769206312.

Arun: Mike -> please attach the initial logs you pulled to the thread. Include a sanitized stacktrace.

Mike: pasting sanitized snippet:
```
14:02:11 ERROR embed-service requestId=abc123 status=500 "S3AccessDenied: Access Denied"
14:02:11 WARN retryer taskId=rt-9845 governor=embed-retryer-3 retry=1 role=embed-retryer-role
14:02:12 INFO role-change trigger=automation user=svc-deploy-bot action=PutBucketAcl bucket=redwood-temp-cache
```

Jenna: that trace shows automated role action immediately after repeated failures. Looks like svc-deploy-bot invoked a remediation which mis-applied an ACL.

Dave: mapped keys -> customers: preliminary mapping shows some customer-owned keys (customer ids: cu_1123, cu_7809) present in redwood-temp-cache. Need to validate if those keys contain raw PII or only embeddings.

Arun: Jenna, can you confirm the type of data stored for those keys? Embeddings are derived but we treat embeddings as potentially sensitive per policy.

Jenna: right. For this cohort, mappings indicate embeddings + metadata (filename, minimal prompts). We need a quick data classification: run `s3select` to inspect a small sample; do not download more than necessary.

Mike: running selective s3select sampling for cu_1123 and cu_7809 (only 10 objects each) now.

Mike: sample results: objects contain embedding vectors + metadata: original filename, customer-annotated tag. No raw free-text prompt bodies in sample.

Jenna: ok that lowers risk but still qualifies as potentially sensitive under our privacy policy. Notify customers as potential exposure of derived embeddings and metadata.

Arun: Sara, can you draft the short customer alert? Keep it concise, explain what we know, actions we've taken, and next steps. Example draft below — use plain language and include contact link and mitigation advice.

Sara: Draft v1 for potentially affected customers:
"Hi — we’re reaching out to let you know we’re investigating a potential exposure involving a subset of embedding data stored in our temporary cache. We have isolated the automation that caused the change, blocked further access, and are performing a scope assessment. At this time we have no evidence of exfiltration. We will provide an update within 60 minutes and will follow up with a detailed notice if your data is confirmed affected. If you have urgent concerns, contact security@redwood.ai."

Jenna: tweak: add data types and timeframe.

Sara: Draft v2 (with tweaks):
"Hi — we’re investigating an incident that may have exposed embedding vectors and metadata for a small set of customers between 2026-04-27 14:00–14:10 UTC. We have isolated the process, disabled the automation, and begun a targeted review. No confirmed data access by third parties at this time. We will update you within 60 minutes and notify you if your account is confirmed affected. For immediate questions, email security@redwood.ai."

Legal-Bot: For customer outbound, avoid language implying actual exposure until confirmed. Use 'potentially affected' and include required data elements per our breach notification checklist: incident id, timeframe, data types, mitigation steps, contact, next update ETA.

Jenna: also preserve logs for audit and regulator timelines. Add retention note.

Arun: agree. Mike, ensure immutable log snapshots saved to secure-storage with chain-of-custody metadata.

Mike: snapshots saved: s3://secure-audit/INC-2026-0427/snap-1769204512.tar.gz (read-only).

Dave: CS-led inbound: please route any customer replies that look for further detail to me and do not speculate. We’ll coordinate with security to draft follow-ups.

Sara: I'll hold the two drafts. Which segment do we send to cu_1123 and cu_7809 now? Short or longer?

Jenna: short alert is fine now; follow with full notice if confirmed. Keep record of sent messages.

Arun: agreed. Mike post the status page update now (include ETA). Sara send short email to the two customers with cc to security and support. Jenna coordinate on the wording.

Mike: Status page posted. Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0427 (interim). Note: ETA next update 60 minutes.

Sara: Sending emails. Using templated subject: "Security notice - Potential impact to embedding data (INC-2026-0427)". Copy below:

--- email body start ---
Hi <Customer>,

We’re contacting you about an ongoing investigation that may involve embedding data and related metadata for a small number of customers between 2026-04-27 14:00–14:10 UTC. We have temporarily isolated the process and blocked further access. At this time we have no evidence of unauthorized access outside our systems.

What we’re doing: targeted review, preserving logs, and preparing a full notification if your data is confirmed affected.

When we’ll follow up: within 60 minutes with an update or sooner if we confirm scope.

Contact: security@redwood.ai
--- email body end ---

Sara: sent to cu_1123 and cu_7809 at 14:17 UTC.

Dave: note: customer cu_7809 replied asking if their raw files were included. I forwarded to Jenna.

Jenna: replied to Dave for the customer: "At this time our sample shows only embeddings + minimal metadata; no raw files seen in the sampled objects. We’re completing full verification and will notify within timeline."

Arun: brief incoming update on scope scan?

Mike: full mapping complete. Affected objects count: 28 for cu_1123, 11 for cu_7809. Data types: embeddings + file name metadata + small tag fields. No raw text blobs found.

Jenna: based on classification, this is a limited exposure of derived vectors + metadata. Regulatory risk moderate — depends on customer vertical. Recommend final customer notice and opt-in to offer extended monitoring.

Legal-Bot: Confirmed: if embeddings are not reversible to raw PII per our tech assessment, we still must notify customers under contractual terms. Regulatory notification not required at this time but escalate if requests from regulators.

Arun: Decision: send final customer notice stating confirmed affected, describe data types, mitigation steps, offer 90 days free monitoring, and include contacts. Legal to approve inbound wording.

Legal-Bot: Approve final wording, recommend including our remediation timeline and root cause summary and removing speculative language. Provide ticket link to support escalation template.

Sara: Final customer notification draft:
"Hello <Customer>,

We’ve completed our investigation into INC-2026-0427 and confirm that embedding vectors and limited metadata for your account were present in the affected temporary cache between 14:00–14:10 UTC on 2026-04-27. We have no evidence of external access beyond the automated remediation worker.

What we did: isolated and disabled the automation, restored correct bucket ACLs, preserved audit logs, and started a targeted review for any downstream exposure.

What you can do: we recommend rotating any keys if you use short-lived tokens tied to embedding ingestion. We are offering 90 days of complimentary monitoring; contact security@redwood.ai to enroll.

If you have questions, reply to this message and we’ll coordinate next steps."

Jenna: approved. Add a short root cause pointer: cause: automated remediation applied overly-broad ACL when handling repeated failures. Mitigation: change automation to use least-privilege and add a safety rollback.

Sara: final notices queued and will be sent in 5m.

Arun: good job. Follow-ups: post-incident actions: 1) modify embed-retryer role to least-privilege, 2) add canary tests for ACL changes, 3) run a sweep for other automation with S3 write perms, 4) update runbook to require human sign-off for ACL changes. Assign owners and due dates within 48h.

Mike: capturing follow-ups in INC-2026-0427 Jira.

Jenna: we’ll schedule a postmortem with privacy and product in 72h.

incident-bot: Handoff reminder: @Arun to @Mike in 30m per schedule.

Arun: handing off now to @Mike for continuity. Mike, you're on for next 4 hours.

Mike: acknowledged. Taking over. Will monitor customer replies and coordinate with security/legal.

Dave: I'll update CS playbook with the final templates and routing rules.

Sara: final notices sent at 14:33 UTC. I'll post delivery receipts to this thread when I have them.

Mike: thread summary for records: isolated automation, disabled job, saved immutable logs, confirmed limited exposure (embeddings + metadata) for two customers, final notice sent, follow-ups created.

Jenna: closing loop — preserve audit timeline and schedule root cause PM.

Arun: thanks team. If anything else pops up, ping this thread or call the oncall number. :thumbsup:
